summary: A wallchart of who is away: one new read endpoint GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar and one new screen at /org/{orgId}/time-off/calendar, rows are active memberships and columns are consecutive calendar days, with a band per approved (solid) or pending (hatched) VacationRequest and holiday/weekend shading. Behind it sits the change that costs the most: a member's holiday country stops being Account.phoneCountryCode and becomes Membership.countryCode falling back to Organization.countryCode — two new nullable columns, one shared helper, and four already-shipping call sites that must all adopt it, two of which move what Amounts Owed pays. Both countries get a picker: the organization's on Settings > Holidays behind a new GET/PUT pair, the member's on their About tab riding the member update that already ships. One new capability in both capability unions, one sidebar row, one additive migration. The calendar writes nothing. REPLAN, round 2: the country-write rule the review halted on is settled in the document - both writes test the uppercase shape AND membership of the assigned ISO 3166-1 list, so an unassigned code such as XX is refused, and both refusals carry PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid rather than HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid, whose text is false of XX. Two code blockers are planned with it: the calendar screen resolves today from the caller's Account.timezone rather than the browser clock, and a failed read is reported as a failed read rather than as an empty scope. REPLAN, round 3: the document settled the picker question the review halted on, and two code blockers are planned with it. Both stated-country pickers now draw COUNTRY_OPTIONS from packages/validation — the same 249 assigned codes rule 9 accepts — so what a picker offers is exactly what its save stores, and the phone-derived list leaves this feature entirely. An absent countryCode key on the organization PUT changes nothing, the same choice the member write beside it makes. The calendar banner draws the endpoint’s own message only from a 422 carrying fields and the shipped generic one on every other outcome, so no framework string reaches the reader. And the loading skeleton carries no length literal of its own: the DS gaps table closes that set at three. REPLAN, round 4: the document settled the last halt in its own text - the organization picker gains a first option meaning "no country", labelled from a new message export, because narrowing that picker to the assigned list had left REQ-01-034 with no control behind it. Two code blockers ride with it, both of them rules round 3 already planned and the diff did not carry: the organization country PUT must decide on the PRESENCE of the countryCode key, the way the member write beside it does, so a keyless or mistyped body changes nothing; and the two helpers §Shared code names - timeOffCalendarToday and resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone - must exist as exports of packages/validation, read by both the endpoint and the screen, with the API’s private restatement of the zone fallback deleted.

tasks.title: Schema and the one migration — two nullable country columns
tasks.detail: Membership.countryCode String? @db.Char(2) and Organization.countryCode String? @db.Char(2) — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, uppercase, nullable with NO default and NO backfill (contracts, Data Model). Doc-comment each the way the neighbouring columns are: Membership's is the first link of the holiday-country chain (REQ-01-026), null meaning 'use the organization's'; Organization's is the second. No new table, no index, no altered column. Write the migration SQL by hand in the style of apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260901130000_spec_org_03_holidays/migration.sql — two ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "countryCode" CHAR(2) statements and a header saying why it is additive. This run writes exactly one migration; do not add a second in any later task.

migration.note: infra/deploy.sh runs infra/migrate.sh as a one-off ECS task on the NEW image (deploy.sh:175-185, guarded on `api` being among the services deployed) and only then `tf apply`s the services (:187-192) — the schema changes while the PREVIOUS code is still serving, which is why the header at deploy.sh:27 states migrations run BEFORE the rollout. Both columns are nullable with no default and nothing backfills them, so old code against the new schema simply never selects them and a code rollback needs no database rollback. tasks.title: packages/validation — the messages, the capability in both unions, the country chain, the range and preset arithmetic
tasks.detail: Four pieces, all in packages/validation because both surfaces re-run them and because npm run test:unit runs this workspace and nothing else. (1) NEW MODULE packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts, beside holiday-messages.ts and re-exported from index.ts: TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES with exactly the eleven rows of the Error Messages table (rangeRequired, rangeInverted, rangeTooWide, scopeInvalid, teamsRequired, peopleRequired, tooManyMembers, emptyStateTitle, emptyStateBody, orgCountryHint, memberCountryDefaultOption), verbatim; TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MAX_RANGE_DAYS = 92 and TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MAX_MEMBERS = 100; the scope union 'all'|'teams'|'people' with its validator (REQ-01-041); a range validator answering Validation Rules 1-4 IN THE TABLE'S ORDER and returning the FIRST failure only (contracts: 'a request that is both inverted and scoped everyone is refused with rangeInverted and nothing else') — it compares raw ISO dates and returns no timezone-shifted instant, which is REQ-01-017's half of the contract and the opposite of validateReportRange; the three window presets (Week, 2 weeks, Month) computed from a firstDayOfWeek of 'Monday'|'Sunday' plus the back/forward/today steps of REQ-01-049, where Week and 2 weeks move one preset length and Month moves a whole calendar month; and a band accessible-name builder in the mock's order ('Vacation · approved · 2026-09-14 – 2026-09-18 · 5 working days'), so no screen writes that string inline. (2) roles.ts: add 'ViewTimeOffCalendar' to the Capability union and to ROLE_CAPABILITIES for admin, manager and user — not viewer. (3) index.ts: add 'view-time-off-calendar' to MemberCapability and write it into all four rows of CAPABILITY_MATRIX (true, true, true, false). Both unions are exhaustive against their tables, so the compiler names every row you miss. (4) reports.ts: export resolveMemberHolidayCountry(membershipCountry, organizationCountry) — both arguments REQUIRED, neither defaulted. It answers REQ-01-026/027/040: return the membership's value when it normalizes to a real ISO alpha-2, else the organization's when it does, else null; the result is always UPPERCASE ('pl' -> 'PL'), and a value that is two letters but not an assigned code ('XX') does NOT normalize. Use validateCountryCode from autofill.ts (packages/validation/src/autofill.ts:683 — it upcases and tests membership of COUNTRY_NAMES, the 249-code list) as the normalizer; do NOT use validateHolidayCountryCode here, which is the WRITE rule and accepts any two uppercase letters. isHolidayApplicableToMember already ships at reports.ts:509 and is unchanged. (5) REPLAN, round 2 - VALIDATION RULE 9, which the contracts settle as TWO tests and not one, exported once and called by both writes: validateStatedCountryCode(input) in packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts. null, undefined and a blank string are valid and normalize to null (REQ-01-034, REQ-01-043); a non-string is invalid; then the UPPERCASE SHAPE, /^[A-Z]{2}$/ against the raw value, so 'pl' is REFUSED rather than upcased (Edge case 11 rests on this); then MEMBERSHIP OF THE ASSIGNED ISO 3166-1 LIST through validateCountryCode (packages/validation/src/autofill.ts:683), so 'XX' is refused though its shape is right (REQ-01-036, REQ-01-051, Edge case 10). Every failure carries PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid ('Enter a valid country', autofill.ts:510) and never HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.countryCodeInvalid, whose text ('must be 2 uppercase letters') is false of the value it would be refusing. COMPOSE validateCountryCode; do not copy COUNTRY_NAMES - one country list, one definition. Do NOT change validateHolidayCountryCode: a holiday ROW's country keeps it (holidays.service.ts:322, HolidayModal.tsx:222), because there the code is a label matched against a resolved country and an unassigned one reaches nobody, which is visible and harmless. These two columns are the INPUT to that resolution, which is why they are the strict ones. REPLAN, round 3 - THE THREE HELPERS THE SETTLED CONTRACT NAMES. §Shared code now lists validateStatedCountryCode(input), timeOffCalendarToday(timezone, instant) and resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone(timezone) beside TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES, so all three are exports of packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts and the endpoint and the screen both read them - one definition of REQ-01-018’s today, not one per surface. timeOffCalendarToday FORMATS THROUGH todayInTimeZone (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:639), which already ships, is exported from the package root and already carries REQ-01-018’s fallback: resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone answers which zone (the stated one when Intl accepts it, UTC when it is null, empty or unrecognized) and todayInTimeZone answers the calendar date in it. Do not restate the en-CA formatting a second time - two implementations of one fallback is where the rule drifts, and nothing observable separates them today. REPLAN, round 4 - THE TWO HELPERS ARE STILL NOT ON DISK, AND THERE IS A TWELFTH MESSAGE. (a) `git grep -n "timeOffCalendarToday\|resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone" -- specs apps packages e2e` answers with the two contract lines and no code: commit c75a6bb deleted both from packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts, which now ends at :257 with validateStatedCountryCode, and the zone fallback was restated privately inside the API instead (time-off-calendar.service.ts:410, reportedTimezone). §Shared code names both as exports beside TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES (contracts:213-214), so write both in packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts and re-export them from the package root the way that module’s other exports already are. resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone(timezone: string | null | undefined): string answers 'UTC' when the value is null, undefined or blank after a trim, and 'UTC' when new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: value }) throws; otherwise the stated value verbatim, unnormalized. timeOffCalendarToday(timezone: string | null | undefined, instant: Date = new Date()): string is ONE LINE: return todayInTimeZone(resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone(timezone), instant). IT MUST DELEGATE - todayInTimeZone (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:639) ships, is exported from the root and already carries the en-CA formatting, so a second Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { year, month, day }) anywhere in this diff is a second implementation of one rule, which is exactly what the named export exists to prevent. Neither helper may live in apps/api or in apps/web: the endpoint and the screen both read them. (b) TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES gains a TWELFTH row, superseding round 2’s "exactly the eleven rows": orgCountryNoneOption, whose text is "No country — global holidays only" (contracts:178). The separator is an EM DASH (U+2014), not a hyphen - copy the row’s own characters, because the static gate matches the table text literally. It labels the first option of org-country-select and is the only thing in the product that clears the organization country (contracts:344-348).

tasks.title: GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar — the read the whole screen is
tasks.detail: Controller: @Controller('api/organizations/:orgId') with @UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard) and one @Get('time-off/calendar') — copy HolidaysController's stack exactly. NO RequireCapability and NO CapabilityGuard: the refusal must be a bare 404 (REQ-01-002) byte-identical to the wrong-organization one (REQ-01-039), and CapabilityGuard answers 403. Gate in the service, in the shape of HolidaysService.requireViewCapability (holidays.service.ts:239): load the caller's membership by session.accountId, refuse a non-active or wrong-organization row, then `if (!can(normalizeRole(caller.role), 'view-time-off-calendar')) throw new NotFoundException()`. NORMALIZE — a membership still storing 'member' must be answered 200 (TC-01-UNIT-04). Every query filters by session.organizationId; the path :orgId is never a selector. Validation runs in the Validation Rules table's order and the FIRST failure is the whole answer, thrown as 422 `{ error: 'validation_error', fields: { <field>: <message> } }` (the shape ReportsService.parseQuery emits at reports.service.ts:615): startDate/endDate -> rangeRequired, range -> rangeInverted then rangeTooWide, scope -> scopeInvalid, projectIds -> teamsRequired, memberIds -> peopleRequired, scope -> tooManyMembers (rule 8, checked last, after the rows resolve). Row resolution: scope=all is every active membership of the caller's organization; scope=teams is every active membership with a ProjectMember row on one of the named projects, PLUS — when projectIds contains the literal sentinel 'none' — every active membership with no ProjectMember row on any NON-ARCHIVED project (REQ-01-007; the named-project branch never consults the archived flag, Edge case 5), duplicates collapsed to one row (Edge case 6); scope=people is the named memberships. Foreign ids are intersected away silently (REQ-01-010) and 'removed' memberships never appear (REQ-01-011). Order by display name case-insensitively (REQ-01-012). Days: compare VacationRequest.startDate/endDate and Holiday.date against UTC-midnight @db.Date bounds built from the raw ISO strings, `new Date(`${iso}T00:00:00.000Z`)`, the way HolidaysService.listHolidays does — never validateReportRange's timezone-shifted startUtc, which is exactly the boundary drop TC-01-INT-10 is built to catch. range.today comes from the caller's Account.timezone via Intl, falling back to UTC when it is null, empty or unrecognized (REQ-01-018, the currentYearIn idiom at holidays.service.ts:358). days[] carries date, isWeekend (Sat/Sun) and isoWeek. Bands: status in (approved, pending) intersecting the window, carrying the TRUE startDate/endDate plus startsBeforeWindow/endsAfterWindow, kind 'vacation', the frozen workingDays (never recounted), and the request id. Holidays: every Holiday dated inside the window whatever its country, each with appliesToAllInView computed against the rows THIS response carries; each member row carries the holidayIds that reached it, resolved server-side through resolveMemberHolidayCountry + isHolidayApplicableToMember, and countryCode = the RESOLVED country. Load the organization's countryCode once per request, not per member. The body carries no financial field and no MemberProfile field (TC-01-INT-01 asserts their absence over the whole body). meta = { scope, memberCount }. Register the controller and the service flat in app.module.ts beside HolidaysController/HolidaysService. T4 adds its own pair to the same two lists — take that edit here if you implement T3 first, and leave the file alone in T4. REPLAN, round 4 - range.today AND range.timezone BOTH COME FROM packages/validation. `today: timeOffCalendarToday(stated)` and `timezone: resolveTimeOffCalendarTimezone(stated)` (T2), and the private reportedTimezone at time-off-calendar.service.ts:407-419 is DELETED with its comment. Round 1’s "via Intl ... the currentYearIn idiom" is superseded: it was right about the answer and wrong about where it is written. After this the service decides nothing about which day today is or which zone it was read in - it imports the two helpers and passes Account.timezone through them.

concurrency.lock: none — the calendar writes nothing (State Machine invariant 1). It reads Membership, ProjectMember, VacationRequest, Holiday and Organization in one request with no transaction; every rule is evaluated on read, so a holiday deleted or a country set between two fetches simply shows in the next one (Edge cases 12, 13, 19).

tasks.title: GET and PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/settings/country — the organization's country
tasks.detail: A pair beside SigningSettingsController, at api/organizations/:orgId/settings/country, guarded by SessionGuard + OrgScopeGuard only. The capability check runs IN THE SERVICE, unlike its signing neighbour, because both halves answer 404 and CapabilityGuard answers 403: `view-holidays` for the GET (REQ-01-047) and `manage-holidays` for the PUT (REQ-01-035), each a bare NotFoundException, the HolidaysService.requireViewCapability / requireManageCapability shape. Both read and write Organization by session.organizationId, never the path id. GET returns { countryCode } — the stored value, null when nobody has stated one. PUT takes { countryCode } where null or '' clears it (REQ-01-034), validates with validateStatedCountryCode (T2, Validation Rule 9 - empty clears; anything else must be exactly two uppercase letters AND a code the assigned ISO 3166-1 list carries, so 'pl' and 'XX' are both refused), refuses a bad one with 422 { error: 'validation_error', fields: { countryCode: PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid } } (REQ-01-036), and returns the same body the GET does, carrying the value now stored. Register both in app.module.ts's controllers and providers (that file is T3's — make the edit in whichever task runs first). REPLAN, round 3 - AN ABSENT countryCode KEY CHANGES NOTHING, and the document now states it twice: REQ-01-034’s Decided ("a body with no countryCode key changes nothing, as the member write beside it does: clearing on an absent key lets a mistyped key drop the country the fallback depends on", spec:359) and the PUT contract ("A body with no countryCode key changes nothing and answers the stored value unchanged", contracts:134). This REVERSES what round 2 planned. PRESENCE DECIDES, and the validator cannot decide it: validateStatedCountryCode(undefined) answers { valid: true, value: null }, so a route that hands it a missing key clears the column on a mistyped body, answers 200, and every member on the organization fallback silently drops to global holidays only. Test the key itself - `'countryCode' in body` on the parsed object, the idiom members.service.ts uses for the same field and HolidaysService.parseInput uses at holidays.service.ts:316 - and when it is absent write nothing at all and answer the stored value with 200. An explicit null or an empty string IS a submission and clears the column (REQ-01-034); anything else is rule 9’s to refuse. The two country writes now make the same choice, and it is the document’s rather than a code comment’s. AUTHORIZATION: both capability checks are handed the NORMALIZED role - can(normalizeRole(caller.role), 'view-holidays') and can(normalizeRole(caller.role), 'manage-holidays'). The database stores admin or member; the target set is admin | manager | user | viewer. 'admin' normalizes to admin and holds both; a stored 'member' normalizes to user, which holds neither, so it is answered 404 on both halves - the same answer a viewer gets, and the same answer the holiday list beside it already gives that row. REPLAN, round 4 - THE ABSENT KEY STILL CLEARS, AND THE FILE ARGUES FOR IT. Round 3 planned this rule and the code did not move: organization-country.service.ts:76 hands (input ?? {}).countryCode straight to validateStatedCountryCode, undefined normalizes to { valid: true, value: null } (packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts:250), :84 writes it, and a body of {} - or a mistyped {"country":"PL"} - answers 200 {"countryCode":null} on an organization that had PL, dropping every member who relied on the second hop of REQ-01-026. TEST THE KEY FIRST, in the exact idiom the member write beside it uses (members.service.ts:454): const wantsCountry = input !== null && typeof input === 'object' && 'countryCode' in input. WHEN IT IS FALSE: touch nothing - no prisma.organization.update and NO organization_country_set log line, because nothing was set - read the stored value with the same select the GET uses and answer 200 { countryCode } unchanged. WHEN IT IS TRUE: exactly what ships today - rule 9, 422 on a refusal, the write, the log line; an explicit null or an empty string IS a submission and clears (REQ-01-034). DELETE the comment at :72-75, which states the reading the document reversed ("An absent countryCode key clears the column, which is the opposite of the member update beside it, and deliberately") - a file may not carry a decision the spec has settled the other way. Put the settled reason in its place: clearing on an absent key lets a mistyped key drop the country the fallback depends on (spec:359, contracts:133-134). The interface comment at :23-26 ("`null` and `''` both clear") is true and incomplete - an absent key is not a submission. DO NOT change validateStatedCountryCode to refuse undefined: normalizing empty, null and undefined to null is the validator’s contract, the member write depends on it for a present key carrying null, and TC-01-UNIT-01’s block asserts it. Presence is the ROUTE’s question, and after this both country routes answer it the same way.

concurrency.lock: none, by REQ-01-033 — last-write-wins on one column with no read-modify-write, so there is nothing to lose. Other writers of this row: SigningSettingsService.update (a different column), and MembersService.remove (members.service.ts:160) and MembersService.updateDetail (members.service.ts:404), both of which hold `SELECT id FROM "Organization" ... FOR UPDATE` for their zero-admin count. A concurrent country write therefore WAITS on one of those transactions and then applies; it never reads the row first, so it cannot lose an update to them.

tasks.title: The member's country on the shipped detail read and write
tasks.detail: Two shipped routes gain one field each and change in no other way — same guards, same statuses, same messages for everything they already carry. READ (getDetail, members.service.ts:312): add countryCode to the MemberDetail interface and to the explicit projection at :352. It is the STORED value, null included, never the resolved one (REQ-01-045), and it is unconditional — the route is gated by no capability and the field is not conditional on one, so a user and a viewer receive it too. WRITE (updateDetail, members.service.ts:390): add countryCode to MemberDetailUpdateInput and write it inside the EXISTING transaction and the existing organization-row FOR UPDATE at :404, adding no lock of its own. Presence decides: touch the column only when the key is present in the body (`'countryCode' in body`, the idiom HolidaysService.parseInput uses at holidays.service.ts:316), so a caller that omits it changes nothing — Backward Compatibility 3. An explicit null or '' stores null (REQ-01-043). Validate with validateStatedCountryCode (T2, Validation Rule 9 - the uppercase shape AND membership of the assigned ISO list, so 'pl' and 'XX' are both refused) and refuse a bad value with 400 { errors: { countryCode: PROFILE_MESSAGES.country.invalid } } (REQ-01-051) — 400, the status this route already refuses an invalid role and an invalid job title with, and the { errors } shape it already uses for jobTitle; NOT the 422 the organization write answers. The whole route stays behind its existing `can(caller.role, 'edit-detail')` check, so a caller without it still gets 403 MEMBER_MESSAGES.editForbidden and the new field buys no new refusal (REQ-01-044). REQ-01-048 needs NO CODE: restore (members.service.ts:273) and the invitation-acceptance restore (invitations.service.ts:529) both write only status/joinedAt/role/jobTitle and neither clears countryCode — keep it that way, and let TC-01-INT-28 be what proves it. Do not add the field to MembersService.list. AUTHORIZATION: this route's gate is shipped and unchanged - can(caller.role, 'edit-detail') at members.service.ts:415, which is handed the RAW stored value. Leave it that way: normalizing it here would change who may edit a member, which is no part of this spec. Both stored values reach the same decision under the target set - 'admin' is spelled identically in both enums and holds edit-detail, and a stored 'member' holds it under neither reading (can('member', ...) is false because CAPABILITY_MATRIX has no 'member' row, and normalizeRole('member') is user, which does not hold edit-detail either). The new field therefore buys no new refusal and no new grant (REQ-01-044).

concurrency.lock: the existing `SELECT id FROM "Organization" WHERE id = ... FOR UPDATE` at members.service.ts:404, inside updateDetail's own $transaction — countryCode is written by the same tx.membership.update as role and jobTitle and adds no lock. Other writers of a Membership row: MembersService.remove (status, under the same organization lock at :160), MembersService.restore (:273), InvitationsService.accept (:504 create, :529 same-organization restore), SignupService and TestMembersController. None of them touches countryCode, which is what REQ-01-048 requires.

After this task no code path resolves a holiday country from Account.phoneCountryCode; the column stays on Account for the phone field that owns it. One implementation of the rule, or REQ-01-026 is true on one screen and false on the others.
allCallSites: apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.service.ts#listHolidays (the scope=mine branch, :98-107) — resolves the country behind the Time Tracking calendar's holiday markers and the vacation-request modal's holiday hint. After: the caller's Membership.countryCode, else the organization's, else null; a null caller still gets every global row, and only that.

apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts#loadCaller (:530-553) — sets Caller.countryCode, which is the country the Time Off 'my' report and the Amounts Owed 'my' roster read. After: the caller's membership country, else the organization's.

After: each membership's own country, else the organization's, else null — which pays LESS than today for a member whose only country was their phone's, and MORE for one who had none and is now covered by the organization's. Both directions are the deploy-day step the README's Blast Radius names; neither is a code decision to make here.

apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts#buildTimeOffResponse (:1875-1886) — the membership-country union behind the Time Off 'organization_wide' holiday group. After: each active membership resolved through the chain; the union of what they resolve to is what that group covers.

concurrency.lock: none — all four are reads. The chain is evaluated on read, which is why setting or clearing either country repairs every reader at once and nothing has to be backfilled (Edge cases 12 and 19).

tasks.title: The calendar screen and the navigation row
tasks.detail: A 'use client' page that fetches /api/organizations/{orgId}/time-off/calendar with credentials 'same-origin' — no server action, no API route. Gate: `if (!can(normalizeRole(session.role), 'view-time-off-calendar')) notFound()`, the notFound() pattern the documents pages use (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/documents/page.tsx:116) rather than the holidays page's redirect, because TC-01-E2E-06 asserts the app's not-found handling. Sidebar: a 'Calendar' row with testId nav-time-off-calendar, href /org/{orgId}/time-off/calendar, pushed into the existing timeOff array ABOVE the Holidays row (Sidebar.tsx:153), gated on hasCapability(role, 'ViewTimeOffCalendar') and omitted otherwise — never drawn-and-disabled. Structure, top to bottom, per the mock and contracts>Screens: PageHeader with the range navigation in its right slot (calendar-prev, calendar-today, calendar-next, calendar-range-label); ReportControls from @devscribed/ds in its scope + children shape, holding TWO ToggleButtons in their `options` form — the three calendar-scope-* segments and the three calendar-window-* segments. Draw no segmented control of your own: ToggleButton owns the track, the pill, --shadow-toggle-active, the roving tab stop and the per-segment data-testid. The teams and people pickers are MultiFilter from apps/web/src/reports/ReportFilters.tsx (a Select isMulti with closeMenuOnSelect false), rendered only for their own scope; calendar-teams-picker lists an 'Unassigned' entry ABOVE the projects whose value is the sentinel 'none', which ticks like a project and may be the only tick. Options come from the shipped GET .../projects and GET .../members. Legend, then the grid. Defaults: scope=all and the Month window over the caller's current month; the range is in-page state and is NOT put in the URL. Window and range arithmetic comes from T2's exported presets, driven by session.account.firstDayOfWeek — Week and 2 weeks step one preset length, Month steps a whole calendar month and always runs first-to-last day of it (REQ-01-049), and calendar-today returns to the window holding today. A band is ONE element spanning every day from its start to its end, weekends and holidays included (REQ-01-023), solid for approved and hatched with a dashed border for pending, carrying T2's accessible name; adjacent bands are separated by their own 3px side margins. A holiday with appliesToAllInView shades the whole column, draws calendar-day-holiday-{date} and NAMES the holiday in calendar-day-header-{date} (REQ-01-030); one without marks only calendar-cell-holiday-{membershipId}-{date} on the members it reached and names nothing in the header (REQ-01-031). Saturday and Sunday columns are shaded from days[].isWeekend (REQ-01-032). No rows -> calendar-empty-state replaces the grid and the filter bar stays (REQ-01-037); rows but no bands -> the full grid, no empty state (REQ-01-038). Any 422 -> calendar-error-banner above the grid carrying the message (the first value of the response's `fields`), with the last good grid left on screen underneath. Loading -> a skeleton in the grid area with the filter bar still interactive. DS GAPS: declare --surface-timeoff-band, --border-timeoff-band, --text-timeoff-band and --name-col: 264px ONCE, in a .time-off-calendar block in apps/web/app/globals.css that also carries what inline styles cannot express — position: sticky on the member column, the horizontal scroll container below --layout-breakpoint-desktop — and read every one of them through var(). No colour and no size on this screen is a literal except the two 3px values the DS gaps table records (the band's side margin and the pending hatch stripe), each carrying a @literal comment with the reason. The band's height is --space-10 and its corner --radius-s. Render exactly the data-testids the contracts table names and no others: the static gate blocks on any data-testid the diff adds that the spec bundle does not name. REPLAN, round 2 - two rules the first pass got wrong. (a) THE ANCHOR IS THE CALLER'S TODAY, NOT THE BROWSER'S. The initial anchor and the calendar-today control both come from todayInTimeZone(session.account.timezone) (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:639, exported from the package root and already used exactly this way at apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/NewRequestModal.tsx:133), whose fallback for a null, empty or unrecognized zone is UTC - REQ-01-018's own fallback, and the same field the server resolves range.today from. A browser-clock anchor puts the today marker in no column at all for a caller whose zone has crossed midnight and the browser's has not, and REQ-01-049 requires the Today control to land on the window HOLDING the caller's today. Nothing about today on this screen is computed from new Date(). (b) A FAILED READ IS NOT AN EMPTY ONE, AND IT NEVER DRAWS THE FRAMEWORK’S OWN WORDS. The banner has exactly TWO branches and no third. A 422 whose body carries `fields` draws the first value of `fields`, which is one of the seven TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES rows the endpoint can answer with. EVERY other outcome - a 404 after a capability was revoked mid-session, a 500, a dropped connection, a body that does not parse, fetch rejecting - draws HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.toastServerError ("Something went wrong. Please try again.", packages/validation/src/holiday-messages.ts), which the contracts’ Error Messages table now carries (contracts:181) and §UI Description assigns to its own state, "Failed for any other reason" (contracts:372). DO NOT chain the response body’s `message` between the two: Nest answers {"message":"Not Found","statusCode":404} and {"message":"Internal server error","statusCode":500}, neither string is an export of packages/validation nor a row of that table, and a chain written `fields ? first : (body?.message ?? generic)` puts a framework string on the reader’s screen while the generic branch behind it never runs. The whole chain is `fields ? Object.values(fields)[0] : HOLIDAY_MESSAGES.toastServerError` and nothing longer. It must equally never carry TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.emptyStateBody, whose table row gives it no route and whose state is Empty (no rows) alone - drawing it on a read that never happened reports a fact about data nobody fetched. The last good grid stays underneath in both branches. (c) NO FOURTH LENGTH LITERAL ON THIS SCREEN. The spec’s DS gaps table closes the set: --surface-timeoff-band, --border-timeoff-band, --text-timeoff-band and --name-col are declared once in the .time-off-calendar block, and the ONLY literals this screen may carry are the 3px band side-margin, the 3px pending-hatch stripe and the 2px today inset, each with an @literal comment and its reason (contracts, DS gaps row 3). The loading skeleton’s placeholders are measured from tokens and from the track they sit in - height var(--space-4), corner var(--radius-s), width from the column - and the name-column placeholder carries NO max-width of its own: `max-width: 160px` is a fourth literal no token names, no @literal comment explains and no DS-gaps row records, and it is the only length in the block that is neither a var() nor a 1px hairline. If that placeholder must read as shorter than its column, express it as a fraction of the track (a percentage), never as a new number of pixels; adding a DS-gaps row instead is a spec edit, which is not this run’s to make. (d) THE SKELETON IS DRAWN IN A GRID OF ITS OWN. It renders only while `loading && !data`, when days[] is empty and a data-derived template declares ONE day column - placing fourteen cells into it creates thirteen implicit auto tracks, and a placeholder’s width: 100% inside an auto track resolves against no definite width. Give the skeleton its own template, var(--name-col) plus exactly the number of day columns it places, so the claim its comment makes - the grid’s own geometry, so the page does not jump when the answer arrives - is true on the only paint it has. No case can catch this one: the contracts record "No case: the skeleton lives between two paints". REPLAN, round 4 - the screen calls the NAMED helper. CalendarScreen.tsx:139 becomes const today = (): string => timeOffCalendarToday(session.account.timezone), importing timeOffCalendarToday from @devscribed/validation in place of todayInTimeZone.
